claims.claim_text: Indexed Lieutenant Colonel Francis P. Miller is a high-confidence match to Francis Pickens Miller.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Lt. Col. OSS. U.S. Representative on Tripartite Control Committee for Operation SUSSEX, London
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact middle name, lieutenant-colonel grade, OSS service, and Operation Sussex papers align with the indexed row.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from exact name expansion, matching lieutenant-colonel rank, and explicit OSS chronology in an authoritative archival finding aid.
claims.temporal_assessment: The finding aid places his OSS service in 1943-1944 and describes related material spanning 1942-1946.
claims.match_notes: No service identifier is exposed or relied on publicly; the indexed Box 524 jacket remains unreviewed.

sources.locator_override: Collection summary page 1; biographical sketch page 3

claims.claim_text: Miller was Organization Director at the Council on Foreign Relations from 1938 through 1941, his best-supported last civilian employer before wartime intelligence service.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Organization Director, Council on Foreign Relations
claims.evidence_paraphrase: An archival chronology dates the role to 1938-1941, the Virginia House lists the same occupation, and a historian places his OSS predecessor work after Pearl Harbor.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence exact-person chronology tied to the distinctive full name and OSS lieutenant-colonel service.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded immediately before the post-Pearl Harbor intelligence chronology; no source literally says recruited from CFR.
claims.match_notes: Separated from his simultaneous elected service in the Virginia House of Delegates.

claims.claim_text: Miller served in the Virginia House of Delegates for Fairfax County through 1941 while also directing organization work at the Council on Foreign Relations.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Official legislative records and an archival biography document the elected role immediately before his wartime intelligence chronology.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence exact-person match supported by full name, career chronology, and OSS rank.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded and simultaneous with CFR employment; treated as a government assignment, not a civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: The official profile lists 1938 and 1940 sessions; the archival chronology summarizes 1938-1941.

claims.claim_text: Miller taught briefly at Yale Divinity School in 1934.
claims.evidence_excerpt: a brief teaching stint at Yale Divinity School in 1934
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Campbell University's summary of a historian's research identifies the institution, work, and year.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Good exact-person match within a continuous Francis Pickens Miller biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment; not the immediate pre-OSS role.
claims.match_notes: Qualified because the accessible source is an institutional summary of a conference paper rather than the underlying personnel record.

claims.claim_text: After teaching at Yale in 1934, Miller worked as a field secretary for the Foreign Policy Association.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Francis P. Miller, ex-official of the Foreign Policy association
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary newspaper corroborates the institutional biography's identification of his Foreign Policy Association work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Good exact-person match corroborated by a contemporary Francis P. Miller reference within his prewar foreign-policy activity.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment; the end date and immediacy are not established.
claims.match_notes: Not promoted to immediate-pre-OSS status; the precise duration remains unknown.
